title: Batch reactor multi-phase sequence with dry-fire protection
nl_spec: Control a batch reactor as a five-phase state machine: 0 = Idle, 1 = Fill, 2 = Heat, 3 = React, 4 = Drain. On StartBatch (when healthy) begin Fill: open the FillValve until the level reaches LVL_HIGH = 80%. Then Heat: run the Heater and Agitator until the temperature reaches TEMP_SET = 100. Then React: keep heating and agitating for PT_REACT = 3 ticks. Then Drain: open the DrainValve until the level falls to LVL_LOW = 5%, returning to Idle. The emergency stop EStop is normally-closed (TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated) and forces Idle with everything de-energized. SAFETY-CRITICAL: the fill and drain valves must never be open together; on emergency stop everything is off; and the heater and agitator must never run unless there is sufficient liquid (Level >= LIQ_MIN = 10) to prevent dry-firing. Use an internal INT State (0..4) and a TON timer. Write an IEC 61131-3 Structured Text PROGRAM named batch_reactor with inputs StartBatch, Level, Temp, EStop and outputs FillValve, Heater, Agitator, DrainValve.

interface.name: EStop
interface.description: Emergency stop, normally-closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = activated

safety_properties.nl: The fill and drain valves are never open at the same time.
On emergency stop, all actuators are de-energized.
The heater never runs without sufficient liquid (dry-fire protection).
The agitator never runs without sufficient liquid.
The heater is never on while the drain valve is open.

scenarios.description: Dry-fire protection: low level inhibits the heater in Heat phase

notes: Five-phase sequence; heater/agitator gated on Level>=LIQ_MIN in their output expressions so the dry-fire property holds even though Level is a free input.
